questions.question_text: In the expression $n + 6$, what does the pronumeral $n$ represent?

options.text: $6$, the number it is added to
options.why: Reads the constant $6$ as the value of $n$ instead of $n$ standing for its own number.

options.text: The letter $n$, used only as a label
options.why: Treats the pronumeral as a name or label rather than a symbol standing for a number.
Confuses the pronumeral with the addition operation written next to it.

questions.question_text: Complete the statement: If a pronumeral represents any number, then we call it a .......... .

options.why: Confuses a pronumeral with many possible values with a constant, which has one fixed value.
Names what a pronumeral represents instead of the term for a pronumeral with many possible values.
Confuses a symbol representing a number with an arithmetic operation.

questions.solution_text: A pronumeral with many possible numerical values is a variable.

questions.question_text:
Complete the statements in order.
(a) Pronumerals are letters or symbols that represent .......... .
(b) If a pronumeral represents any number, then we call it a .......... .
(c) Algebra involves using .......... to represent numbers so we can quickly communicate mathematical relationships.

options.why: Says pronumerals represent operations instead of numbers in the first statement.
Uses constant instead of variable for a pronumeral with many possible values in the second statement.
Uses operations instead of pronumerals for the symbols representing numbers in the third statement.
